12-084.r: Correct: Bhaja (Pune) → Buddhist caves; Sittanavasal → Jain cave temple (Pallava Mahendravarman I). Wrong: Besnagar → Bhagavata cult, Heliodorus' Garuda pillar, not a Shaivite cave. Two pairs.

12-085.r: Sun Temple → Konark; Lingaraja Temple → Bhubaneswar; Hawa Mahal → Jaipur; Gomateshwara statue → Shravanabelagola (Karnataka).

12-086.r: Sun temple → Arasavalli (Andhra Pradesh, 7th century, Eastern Ganga king Devendra Verma). Omkareshwar → Shiva Jyotirlinga on the Narmada; Amarkantak → source of Narmada, Son, Johila.

12-087.r: Nalanda → University; Sarnath → Ashoka Pillar; Sanchi → Stupa; Konark → Sun Temple.

12-088.r: Takshashila (Rawalpindi district, Punjab, Pakistan) → between the Indus and Jhelum rivers; founded in the 6th or 7th century BC.

12-089.r: Sonagiri (Digambar Jain site, MP) → 103 Jain temples, 15 km from Datia; main temple No. 57 of Lord Chandraprabhu.

12-091.r: Dilwara Jain temples → Mount Abu (Aravalli hills), Rajasthan.
12-091.t: Not Palitana, Sonagiri or Girnar, which are other Jain centres.

12-094.r: Virupaksha Temple → Hampi, Karnataka; dedicated to Shiva, known there as Virupaksha.

12-095.r: Nagara (North India), Dravida (South India) and Vesara (mix of both) → the three main styles of Indian temple architecture.

12-096.r: Panchayatana → temple style with a central shrine and four subsidiary shrines (Pancha = five); e.g. Kandariya Mahadeo, Lingaraja, Dashavatara (Deogarh).

12-097.r: Naimisharanya → Sitapur district, UP; where Sage Dadhichi gave his bones to make Indra's Vajra.

12-098.r: Correct: Buddha's Mahaparinirvana image → Ajanta (cave 26); Arjuna's Penance / Descent of Ganga → Mamallapuram. Wrong: huge Varaha image is at Udayagiri caves (MP), not Mount Abu.

12-099.r: Chitrakoot → Hindu pilgrimage site spread over UP and MP (district in UP; Kamadgiri temple area in both); BPSC accepted Madhya Pradesh.
12-099.c: Answer not printed; the question names no specific temple and the site lies in both UP and MP.

12-100.r: Earliest → rock-cut elephant at Dhauli (Ashoka, 3rd century BC); then Udayagiri Varaha (5th century AD), Mahabalipuram (7th-8th century), Lingaraja (10th-11th century).

13-001.r: Chola Empire (imperial Cholas) → founded by Vijayalaya in the 9th century (850 AD).

13-003.r: Brihadeeswara temple, Thanjavur → built under Rajaraja I; Chola Dravida style; largest, tallest temple of India; its monolithic Nandi is India's tallest.

13-005.r: Rajaraja I → destroyed the Chera navy at Trivandrum (Kandalur Salai) and captured Pandya king Amarabhujanga; took title 'Mummudi Cholan'.

13-006.r: Chola empire → Coromandel coast and parts of the Deccan (Tungabhadra to Krishna); centres Uraiyur, Kaveripattinam, Thanjavur.

13-007.r: Chola capital → Tanjore (Thanjavur); later Gangaikondacholapuram; Sangam-era Chola capital was Uraiyur.
13-007.h: Capitals in order U-T-G: Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram.

13-008.r: Special feature of Chola administration → autonomy of village administration through village assemblies.

13-015.r: Uttaramerur inscription → details of Chola village administration; each village had its own self-governing 'Sabha' with executive committees.

13-016.r: Chola Variyams (village committees): Thotta → gardens; Eri → tanks and water supply; Pon → gold/finance; Samvatsara → annual committee.

13-017.r: Both true: Cholas beat Pandyas and Cheras to dominate the peninsula (Parantaka I 'Madurai-Kond'; Rajaraja I beat Chera navy); Rajendra I sent an expedition against the Sailendra empire.

13-018.r: Chola bronze Nataraja (Shiva) → always shown with four hands; called the world's greatest iconographic creation of South Indian sthapatis.

13-022.r: Dakshinamurti form of Shiva → Shiva as teacher (Guru) giving knowledge; idol faces south.

13-023.r: Nataraja → dancing Shiva with four hands in a halo (damru upper right, fire upper left, abhayamudra); man's earring right, woman's left (Ardhanarishwara). Both correct.

13-024.r: Kulottunga I (Chola) → sent a goodwill mission of 72 traders to China in 1077 AD.

13-025.r: Cholas → the South Indian power famous for its navy; conquered Ceylon and raided Srivijaya and the Maldives.

13-026.r: Chola emperors usually named their Yuvraj (heir) during their own reign; some other dynasties also did so.
13-026.c: Answer not printed; book says Cholas generally did this but other empires did too.

13-027.r: Rajendra I → made the Bay of Bengal a 'Chola Lake'; beat Mahipal, took title Gangaikonda Chola; founded Gangaikonda Cholapuram; built Chola Gangam lake.

13-030.r: Rajaraja I (accession 985 AD) → first Chola king to create a Naval Army; began the Chola golden era.

13-031.r: Rajaraja I → conquered northern Sri Lanka, destroying Anuradhapura; his son Rajendra I took the whole of Ceylon, defeating Mahinda V.
13-031.t: Northern part only = Rajaraja I; whole Ceylon = Rajendra I.

13-033.r: Rajendra I (Chola) → successful naval campaign (1025 CE) against Srivijaya and Kadaram (Kedah).

13-034.r: Kulottunga I → accepted Sri Lanka's independence under Vijayabahu and married his daughter to Sinhala prince Virapperumal.

13-035.r: More is known of Cholas than earlier dynasties because Rajaraja I began, and later kings continued, inscribing victory narratives on temple walls; A and R true, R explains A.

13-036.r: Eripatti → land whose revenue maintained the village tank; Ghatikas → colleges attached to temples. Taniyurs → very large villages run as single units, not Brahmin gifts.

13-037.r: Foreign-trade guilds → Nanadesis and Manigrama (big early-medieval trading bodies); Sreni = traders-artisans' association; Nagaram = local merchants' body. Both (c), (d).

13-038.r: Tagara → trade centre on the route linking Kalyana and Vengi.

13-039.r: Greatest Chalukya king → Pulakesin II (610-642 AD); Aihole inscription tells his achievements.

13-040.r: Chalukyas → gave women high posts: Vijaya Bhattarika (queen of Chandraditya) issued copper plates and ran administration; Kumkumdevi's advice led to a grant.

13-041.r: Chalukya capital → Vatapi (now Badami, Bagalkot district, Karnataka); Pulakesin I was the real founder.

13-042.r: Aihole inscription (by Ravikirti, for Pulakesin II) → mentions poet Kalidasa (and Bharavi).

13-044.r: Pallava Narasimhavarman I 'Mahamalla' (630-668 AD) → sent two naval expeditions to Ceylon in 642 AD; destroyed Vatapi, took title 'Vatapikonda'.

13-045.r: 'Yavanapriya' (dear to the Yavanas) → Indian black pepper, prized in Roman cookery.

13-046.r: Halbi (Bastar, Chhattisgarh) → eastern Indo-Aryan language between Oriya and Marathi; written in Oriya and Devanagari scripts.

13-047.r: Tolkappiyam (by Tolkappiyar, disciple of Agastya) → oldest available Tamil text, on grammar and poetry; from the 2nd Sangam.

13-048.r: Tolkappiyam → oldest extant Tamil grammar; three parts: Ezhuttu (letter), Col (word), Porul (subject matter).

13-050.r: Silappadikaram → by Ilango Adigal (grandson of Chola king Karikal); story of Kannagi and her husband Kovalan.

13-051.r: Thirukural → philosophy; Tolkappiyam → grammar; Silapadikaram → love story; Manimekalai → merchant story.

13-052.r: Tirumurai → twelve-volume Tamil collection of Shaiva saints' hymns (6th-11th century CE), called the Fifth Veda; basis of Saiva Siddhanta.

13-054.r: Sangam poets knew the Varna classification; Sangam poems also describe material culture, warrior ethic and magical forces.

13-055.r: Arikamedu (Pondicherry) → Indo-Roman trade station; Augustus intaglio, Roman beads; 'Poduke' in the Periplus; Dubreuil called it 'a true Roman city'.

13-059.r: Amphora → tall jar with a narrow neck and two handles; Roman container for wine or oil.

13-060.r: Sangam literature mentions Chola, Chera and Pandya; the Kadamba dynasty is not mentioned.

13-061.r: Sangam Age rulers of the Tamil country → Chera, Chola, Pandya; Pallavas were not.
13-061.t: Pallavas came later; don't add them to the Sangam trio.

13-062.r: Kural (also 'Muppal') → Tamil text by Tiruvalluvar; ethical Bible / Laghuveda of Tamil literature.

13-063.r: Tamil text called 'Laghuveda' → Kural by Thiruvalluvar.

13-064.r: Vattakirutal (Sangam poems) → ritual suicide by a defeated king fasting to death.

13-066.r: Siddhas (Tamil) → monotheistic, condemned idolatry; Lingayats (Kannada) → questioned rebirth and caste, backed widow remarriage. Both correct.

13-067.r: Gupta → Deogarh; Chandela → Khajuraho; Chalukya → Badami; Pallava → Panamalai.

13-068.r: Manigramam → corporation (guild) of merchants in South India, like Nanadesi and Valanjiyar.

13-069.r: Battle of Takkolam → Chola prince Rajaditya (son of Parantaka I) vs Rashtrakuta king Krishna III leading western Gangas and Vaidumbas.

13-070.r: End of Cholas → Hoysalas and Pandyas defeated Rajendra III (c. 1250 AD); dynasty ended c. 1279 AD; Malik Kafur came later (c. 1310 AD).
13-070.c: Answer not printed; by the explanation none of the listed invaders ended the Chola dynasty.

13-071.r: Uraiyur (Sangam era, on the Cauvery, Tiruchirappalli) → major cotton trade centre; mentioned in the Periplus.

13-072.r: Udiyanjiral → Chera king (Kerala), first historical king of the Sangam age; legend says he fed the Mahabharata war fighters.
